en.name: Pasta, dry (no egg)
en.summary: Plain dry pasta — semolina and water, no egg — is one of the most stable things in a kitchen: about 2 years from purchase sealed, and about 1 year once the packet is opened and it goes into a jar. It is the reference other dried noodles on this site are measured against.
en.pantry: Keep it in an airtight jar in a cool, dark, dry cupboard: 2 years from purchase, and about 1 year once opened. There is nothing in it for anything to work on beyond starch and a little protein, and with the water removed it simply sits there. Damp is the one real threat — pasta stored in a humid cupboard will eventually mould or draw pantry moths — followed by smell transfer, since dry pasta takes up odours from soap, spices and detergent through a loose packet. Do not store it above the hob, where steam and heat both reach it.
en.fridge: Dry pasta does not belong in the fridge; it is a dry good and a fridge is humid. The only reason to consider it is a kitchen so hot and damp that the cupboard is not reliable, and then the container must be genuinely airtight and brought back to room temperature before opening. Cooked pasta is a different food entirely: cool it quickly, keep it covered at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and do not leave a pot of cooked pasta standing warm, which is the same hazard as cooked rice.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is given for dry pasta and it needs none — two years in a cupboard already outlasts almost any household's stock. Freezing a sealed bag is a reasonable way to kill pantry-moth eggs in a bulk purchase, but it is a pest measure and not a shelf life. Cooked pasta and filled fresh pasta are the forms worth freezing.
spoilage: A musty or damp smell in the packet, or pasta that has gone soft rather than snapping.
Webbing, small moths, larvae or fine dust — the classic pantry-moth signs.
A smell of soap, spice or detergent picked up in storage.
Visible mould, which means the packet got wet.
tips: Decant into airtight jars; the cardboard box is not a storage container.
Keep pasta away from soap and strong spices — it absorbs smells.
Rotate by date; the shape you never cook is the one that gets the moths.
Check the jar for webbing before cooking from a long-open packet.

faq.q: How long does dry pasta keep?
faq.a: About 2 years from purchase sealed, and about 1 year once the packet is opened and kept airtight.
Rarely, if it stays dry. Damp, mould and pantry moths are the real reasons to throw it out, not age alone.
No. A fridge is humid; an airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard is the right place.

zh.name: 乾燥義大利麵（無蛋）
zh.summary: 純粹的乾燥義大利麵——粗粒小麥粉加水、不含蛋——是廚房裡最穩定的東西之一：未開封從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後裝罐約 1 年。本站其他乾麵類的數字，多半就是以它為基準。
zh.pantry: 裝密封罐放陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃：從購買日起算 2 年，開封後約 1 年。除了澱粉和少量蛋白質之外，它沒有什麼可供微生物利用的東西，水分又已抽乾，所以它就只是安靜地待著。唯一真正的威脅是受潮——放在潮濕櫥櫃裡的麵最後會發霉或招來穀蛾——其次是吸味，因為乾麵隔著鬆口的包裝也會吸附肥皂、香料和清潔劑的氣味。不要放在爐台上方，那裡蒸氣和高溫都到得了。
zh.fridge: 乾麵不該放冰箱；它是乾貨，而冰箱潮濕。唯一值得考慮的情況，是廚房濕熱到櫥櫃不可靠，而那時容器必須真的密封，開封前也要先回到室溫。煮過的義大利麵則完全是另一種食物：請快速降溫、加蓋放 4 °C 以下，不要讓一鍋熟麵溫溫地放著——那和熟飯是同一種風險。
zh.freezer: 乾麵沒有給冷凍數字，也不需要——櫥櫃裡的兩年已經超過幾乎所有家庭的庫存週轉。把密封袋冷凍是處理大量採購穀蛾卵的合理做法，但那是防蟲措施而不是保存期限。真正值得冷凍的是煮好的麵，以及包餡的生鮮義大利麵。
spoilage: 袋內聞到潮霉味，或麵條變軟、折不斷。
出現絲網、小蛾、幼蟲或細粉屑——典型的穀蛾跡象。
吸到了肥皂、香料或清潔劑的氣味。
看得見霉，代表包裝曾經受潮。
tips: 倒進密封罐；紙盒不是保存容器。
遠離肥皂和重味香料——乾麵很會吸味。
依日期輪替；你最少煮的那個形狀，就是最容易長蟲的那一包。
開封很久的包裝，煮之前先檢查有沒有絲網。

faq.q: 乾燥義大利麵可以放多久？
faq.a: 未開封從購買日起算約 2 年，開封後密封保存約 1 年。
保持乾燥的話很少壞。受潮、發霉和穀蛾才是該丟掉的理由，單純放久並不是。
不需要。冰箱潮濕；密封罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃才對。
